findings.reason: naming `read_state` as the classifier's input makes it extend the existing parser instead of re-parsing HTML for the same units, and closes the one reuse gap in an otherwise complete search map (`plan_review.py` fingerprint, `measure_review_cycles.py`, `review_tiers.py`, `recovery.py`), `dispatch._done_when_plan_overlap_warning`).
findings.text: the classifier is specified as taking two plan documents, but `_plan_html.read_state` already parses questions, options, the chosen value, gates, section records and links into a state mapping the classifier must compare; §2 cites only `structured_section_spans` for the done-when reader and never names `read_state` as the classified structure

findings.reason: a second hand-kept scalar list drifts from the fingerprint's, so a `plan-review-hold` meta or a future server scalar would move the fingerprint and earn a review of content nobody changed — exactly the defect §1 measures.
findings.text: §2 defines bookkeeping as "the server-managed scalars the fingerprint already normalises out" and §9 adds `plan-review-hold` "normalised out of the fingerprint like the other server scalars", but neither section names `PLAN_METADATA_SCALARS`/`PLAN_DERIVED_SCALARS` (with `RUN_COMMENT_PREFIX`) as the owner the classifier must read, and `classify_revision` has no named home module

findings.reason: under cli_options 317 each added option/op must be accounted for in the section's own text; §2 already models the required move ("moves to it rather than keeping its own"), so §3/§7/§9 are the inconsistent ones and would gain one accounting line each.
findings.text: §7 adds a migration command with `--write`, §3 adds `--force` to `crew review-plan`, and §9 adds `hold_review`/`release_review` to the `edit_plan` op vocabulary, and no section names what interface it retires or merges, or states why nothing can be

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — `classify_revision` hides a document diff and three classes behind one function, and §5's store reader hides committed-vs-staging resolution and the join behind `select_review_for_head`/`list_plan_reviews`; both are deep, not spread.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §2's bookkeeping class and §9's `plan-review-hold` both re-derive the fingerprint's exclusion set owned by `reckon/crew/plan_review.py:71`, without naming it as the owner to extend.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 1481, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §3 adds `--force`, §7 adds a migration command with `--write`, §9 adds two `edit_plan` ops, and none names what it retires or merges, or why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §2 specifies `classify_revision(before, after)` without citing `reckon/_plan_html.py:852 read_state`, the parser that already yields the decision questions/options/choice, gates, declarations and links the classifier must diff.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §3 extends the existing gate (`reckon/crew/routing.py:2601 require_plan_reviewed`), sweep and `crew review-plan` verb rather than adding a parallel path, and §8 extends `_review_dispatch_fields` in place; no unjustified wrapper is added.
